fields.name: Australia
fields.tagline: Top-tier research universities & vibrant post-study work rights
fields.description:
Australia is one of the world's most popular study destinations for Nepali students. It offers globally ranked universities, a welcoming environment, and generous post-study work rights that let you gain valuable international experience after graduation.

From the sandstone campuses of Sydney and Melbourne to the modern libraries of Perth and Brisbane, Australian institutions combine research excellence with strong industry links, making degrees highly recognised by employers worldwide.
fields.highlights: World-class universities; Strong post-study work rights; Multicultural student cities; High employability

fields.name: United Kingdom
fields.tagline: Prestigious historic institutions & focused 1-year master's degrees
fields.description:
The United Kingdom is home to some of the world's oldest and most prestigious universities. A UK degree is globally recognised and highly valued by employers across every industry.

With focused one-year taught master's programmes, a Graduate Route visa for post-study work, and scholarships at every level, the UK offers exceptional value for ambitious students.
fields.highlights: World-renowned academic heritage; 1-year master's programs; Graduate Route visa; Strong alumni networks

fields.name: Canada
fields.tagline: Co-op work programs, welcoming communities & direct post-study pathways
fields.description:
Canada combines world-class education with one of the most welcoming and diverse societies in the world. Students benefit from work-integrated co-op programmes that build real experience while you study.

A post-graduation work permit of up to three years and clear pathways to permanent residency make Canada a strategic destination for long-term career growth.
fields.highlights: Co-op & paid internships; Welcoming, safe communities; PGWP of up to 3 years; PR pathways for graduates
fields.work_rights: Post-graduation work permit up to 3 years

fields.name: USA
fields.tagline: World-renowned Ivy League & state universities with diverse scholarships
fields.description:
The United States hosts more top-ranked universities than any other country, with unmatched research funding, cutting-edge technology, and a flexible education system.

Students can benefit from OPT work authorisation after graduation and a vast alumni network that opens doors to global careers in technology, business, medicine and academia.
fields.highlights: Ivy League & top research universities; Huge scholarship pool; OPT work authorisation; Diverse career scopes

fields.name: New Zealand
fields.tagline: Quality education in balanced, safe environments with generous post-study opportunities
fields.description:
New Zealand blends high-quality education with one of the safest, most beautiful environments on earth. The education system is globally respected and strongly focused on practical, research-based learning.

With generous post-study work rights and a welcoming culture, New Zealand is a fantastic choice for students who value safety, nature and real-world skills.
fields.highlights: Safe and peaceful environment; Internationally recognised degrees; Post-study work rights; Strong outdoor lifestyle

fields.name: Japan
fields.tagline: High-tech academic programs, rich culture, and booming engineering & business careers
fields.description:
Japan is a global leader in engineering, robotics, business and technology. Japanese universities welcome international students with a system that blends cutting-edge research with deep cultural tradition.

Part-time work allowance, generous scholarship programs and rapid growth of English-taught degree programs make Japan a strategic and affordable choice for ambitious students.
fields.highlights: World leader in technology & engineering; Rich cultural experience; Affordable tuition; Growing career opportunities

fields.name: South Korea
fields.tagline: Cutting-edge technology campuses, affordable tuition and thriving global industries
fields.description:
South Korea is a technology and innovation powerhouse, home to campuses that mix futuristic facilities with a deep culture of academic excellence.

With affordable tuition, generous government scholarships and English-taught programs at major universities, Korea is an increasingly popular destination for international students.
fields.highlights: Global tech & innovation hub; Affordable tuition & scholarships; English-taught programs; Safe modern cities
fields.work_rights: Part-time work permitted for D-2 visa holders

fields.name: Europe
fields.tagline: Affordable tuition, rich history and English-taught programs across Germany, Ireland & France
fields.description:
Europe offers an extraordinary mix of world-renowned universities, affordable (often tuition-free) public education and rich cultural heritage.

Germany, Ireland and France all provide English-taught programs, generous scholarship opportunities and pathways to long-term residency for graduates.
fields.highlights: Low-cost / tuition-free public universities; English-taught programs; Rich cultural heritage; Strong post-study options
fields.work_rights: Post-study work rights vary by country

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
The Australian education system is built around the Australian Qualifications Framework (AQF), which connects the country's school, vocational and university sectors so students can move between levels without losing credit.

After primary and secondary schooling, students can choose between universities, Vocational Education and Training (VET) providers, and private colleges — each with clear pathways into work or further study. Australian qualifications are recognised worldwide and widely respected by employers.

International students are welcomed at every level, from English language programs through undergraduate degrees to doctoral research, with strong support services on campus and a genuinely multicultural student community.

fields.heading: ELICOS & English Language Courses
fields.body:
ELICOS (English Language Intensive Courses for Overseas Students) programs help international students build the English skills they need before entering a VET or university course. Providers range from dedicated language colleges to English centres attached to major universities.

Courses cover General English, Academic English, and IELTS/PTE preparation, with continuous assessment and a direct pathway into your chosen program. Most students study for 8–20 weeks depending on their current level and target entry requirements.

fields.heading: Vocational Education & Training
fields.body:
VET courses are delivered by TAFE and private colleges and are intensely practical, covering fields such as commercial cookery, hospitality, IT, aged care, automotive and project management.

Certificates, diplomas and advanced diplomas can be completed in 1–2 years and typically include hands-on placements. Many VET graduates move directly into Australian employment, and diplomas often provide credit towards a university degree.

fields.heading: University Education
fields.body:
Australian bachelor's degrees take 3–4 years, master's programs 1–2 years, and doctoral studies 3–4 years. Group of Eight universities lead global rankings, while a broader network of modern institutions offers excellent teaching and industry links.

Degrees are taught in English, combine theory with practical placement, and carry strong global recognition — consistently placing Australian graduates among the most employable in the world.

fields.heading: Why Students Choose Australia
items: Globally ranked universities with strong research output
Generous post-study work visa of 2–4 years
Safe, multicultural cities ranked among the most liveable in the world
High graduate employability and an English-speaking workplace
Work rights for international students during study

items: Valid passport with at least 6 months validity

Statement of Purpose and references (if requested)

items: Collect your Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) from the university
Create an ImmiAccount and lodge your visa application online

Travelling and living rights apply for the full duration of study

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
The UK education system is one of the oldest and most respected in the world. Compulsory schooling runs in Key Stages from age 5 to 16, after which students sit GCSEs and typically continue to A-levels or vocational qualifications.

Higher education is delivered by more than 150 universities, from historic Russell Group institutions to modern universities, plus further education colleges that offer foundations and pathway programs.

Degrees are internationally recognised and famous for their focus, depth and rigour — including the distinctive one-year taught master's degree.

fields.heading: Primary & Secondary Education
fields.body:
International students can join British independent schools from primary level onwards. Many families enrol students for GCSEs (ages 14–16) and A-levels (ages 16–18), which are the standard route into UK universities.

Boardings and day schools provide strong pastoral care, small classes and a broad curriculum that develops academic success alongside confidence and leadership.

fields.heading: Further Education
fields.body:
Further education (FE) colleges offer A-levels, BTECs, foundation courses and HND/HNC qualifications. They are ideal for students who want a pathway into university or a vocational start to their career.

International students often begin with an International Foundation Year or Pre-Master's at an FE college or pathway provider before progressing to a degree at a partner university.

fields.heading: Higher Education
fields.body:
UK bachelor's degrees typically take 3 years (4 in Scotland and many sandwich/integrated courses), while taught master's degrees are completed in just 1 year — a fast track to world-class qualifications and lower total cost.

The Graduate Route allows graduates to live and work in the UK for 2 years (3 for PhD) after completing a degree, gaining valuable international experience.

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
Canada's education system is decentralised, with each province managing its own schools, colleges and universities to a consistently high standard. Degrees and diplomas from Canadian institutions are valued worldwide.

Students can choose between universities (theory and research focused), colleges and polytechnics (practical and career focused), and pathway programs that blend both. The system is strongly work-integrated, with co-op terms built into many curricula.

fields.heading: Co-op Programs & Work-Integrated Learning
fields.body:
Co-op (cooperative education) is one of Canada's biggest advantages. Students alternate academic terms with paid placements at partner employers, graduating with up to a year or more of real Canadian work experience.

Many diploma and degree programs at institutions such as Seneca, UBC and the University of Toronto include paid co-op terms, making graduates highly sought after and improving their post-graduation work permit outcomes.

fields.heading: Colleges, Polytechnics & Universities
fields.body:
Canadian colleges and polytechnics offer 1–3 year diplomas and graduate certificates in areas like data analytics, business, IT and health sciences, often with built-in co-op placements.

Universities offer bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees with strong research excellence. Both routes are equally respected and feed into the same post-graduation work permit and permanent residency pathways.

fields.heading: Admission Procedure
items: Research colleges and universities offering your field
Review program entry requirements and intakes
Prepare documents — transcripts, SOP, English test
Apply online and pay the application fee
Receive an offer of admission and confirm acceptance

fields.heading: Application Checklist

fields.heading: Study Permit (Visa)
items: Get your Letter of Acceptance from a designated institution
Apply online to Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC)
Provide biometrics and financial proof
Complete a medical exam if required
Receive a decision — typically 4–8 weeks
Present your port-of-entry letter at arrival

fields.heading: Pathways to Permanent Residency
items: Complete your studies, then work under a PGWP (up to 3 years)
Gain Canadian work experience to boost CRS points for Express Entry
Apply through Provincial Nominee Programs (e.g. OINP, BCPNP)
Qualify under Canadian Experience Class after full-time work
Post-graduation work experience counts strongly for PR

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
The US hosts more of the world's top-ranked universities than any other country, with unmatched research funding and a flexible education system. Students can shape their own degree through majors, minors and electives.

Undergraduate study is typically 4 years and postgraduate study 1–2 years, with huge choice between public state universities, prestigious private research universities and small liberal arts colleges.

fields.heading: Community Colleges & Pathway Programs
fields.body:
Community colleges offer affordable 2-year associate degrees and transfer pathways into four-year universities — a popular, cost-effective route for international students that can save thousands on tuition.

They also provide intensive English programs and smaller class sizes, making them an excellent first step into the US education system before transferring credits to a university degree.

fields.heading: Universities, Colleges & Liberal Arts
fields.body:
Private and public universities range from Ivy League institutions to state flagships renowned for specific disciplines such as engineering, business and computer science.

Liberal arts colleges emphasise broad critical thinking and strong faculty relationships, while research universities offer cutting-edge labs and hundreds of specialisations at every level.

Prepare your English test score (IELTS / PTE) as required

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
New Zealand's education system is globally respected, blending high academic standards with a focus on practical, research-based learning. NCEA in high school leads into universities, institutes of technology or private training establishments.

The country's eight universities all rank internationally, and its polytechnics offer highly practical diplomas that connect directly with employers.

fields.heading: Pathways & Vocational Training
fields.body:
Pathway and vocational programs, such as graduate diplomas in IT and business, offer multiple monthly intakes and strong academic support — ideal for students seeking faster, more affordable outcomes.

These pathways often progress into postgraduate study or directly into New Zealand employment, and count toward post-study work visa eligibility.

fields.heading: Safety & Lifestyle
items: Consistently ranked among the safest countries in the world
Outdoor adventure capital — beaches, mountains and national parks
Friendly, welcoming and inclusive culture
Clean and well-managed student cities
Strong support for international students

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
Japan is a world leader in technology, engineering, robotics and business, and its universities blend cutting-edge research with a deep culture of academic excellence.

The system spans Japanese-language courses in language schools, focused vocational and technical colleges, undergraduate and graduate degrees — many now taught entirely in English at leading universities.

fields.heading: English-Taught Programs (G30 & Beyond)
fields.body:
A growing number of Japanese universities offer full English-taught degrees through the Global 30 (G30) project and similar initiatives, covering engineering, business, economics and international relations.

These programs welcome international students without requiring Japanese, while students can still learn Japanese as part of the experience — a powerful combination for careers in Asia.

fields.heading: Japanese Language Schools
fields.body:
Language schools across Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto offer intensive Japanese courses that serve as a bridge into university study, employment or long-term residency.

Classes typically run for 1–2 years with student-visa support, multiple intake points (April and October), and direct progression to higher education.

fields.heading: Scholarships (MEXT & Others)
items: MEXT government scholarship for degree students
JASSO student support and interest-free loans
University tuition waivers for international students
Private foundations and corporate fellowships
Part-time work to cover living costs

Complete the entrance screening and entrance exam
Receive your admission result

fields.heading: Student Visa & COE
items: The school applies for a Certificate of Eligibility at immigration
Receive your COE — usually within 1–3 months
Apply for your student visa at the Japanese embassy

Renew your visa before expiry during your studies

items: Work part-time up to 28 hours per week with a permit

Pathway to a work visa after graduation

fields.heading: Education System
fields.body:
South Korea is a technology and innovation powerhouse whose universities mix futuristic campuses with a deep culture of academic excellence.

International students are welcomed into Korean-taught and English-taught programs across undergraduate and graduate levels, with globally renowned institutions in the capital Seoul and beyond.

fields.heading: English-Taught Programs
fields.body:
Major universities including Seoul National, Korea and Yonsei offer a wide range of English-taught degrees and exchange programs, enabling international students to study without prior Korean language skills.

These programs combine a globally respected education with Korean cultural immersion — and students are encouraged to add Korean language study through university language institutes.

fields.heading: Scholarships (GKS & University Grants)
items: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) for full degree study
Korean government support for international students
University merit scholarships and tuition waivers
TOPIK-based tuition benefits at many schools

fields.heading: Language & TOPIK
items: TOPIK levels unlock scholarships and tuition discounts
University language institutes teach Korean to proficiency
English-taught tracks require no TOPIK to start
Cultural immersion programs across Seoul campuses

fields.body: Talk to our Korea experts about GKS scholarships, English-taught degrees and your D-2 visa pathway.

fields.heading: A Continent of Education Systems
fields.body:
Europe offers an extraordinary mix of world-renowned universities, affordable public education and rich cultural heritage — with English-taught programs available across Germany, Ireland, France, the Netherlands and more.

The European Higher Education Area standardises bachelor's (3–4 years), master's (1–2 years) and doctoral cycles, and the Schengen area lets students travel freely across 27 countries while they study.

fields.heading: Germany — Tuition-Free Public Universities
fields.body:
Most German public universities charge no tuition — only a small semester fee of around EUR 250–500 that covers transport and student services.

Institutions such as the Technical University of Munich rank at the very top of European engineering and management studies, and scholarships like DAAD support international students throughout their degree.

fields.heading: Ireland — An English-Speaking Hub
fields.body:
Ireland combines first-class, fully English-taught universities with strong post-study work rights and a booming tech and pharmaceutical economy.

Institutions like University College Dublin offer rich campus life, and Irish graduates benefit from an extended stay scheme that supports employment after study.

fields.heading: Scholarships & Funding
items: DAAD scholarships for study in Germany
French government and embassy awards
Irish and EU mobility scholarships
Tuition-free seats at German public universities

fields.heading: Admission Procedure
items: Choose your country, university and program
Check academic equivalence and eligibility
Prepare documents with certified translations
Apply via uni-assist, embassy or the university portal
Receive your admission offer
Arrange visa, accommodation and enrolment

items: Valid passport
Notarised academic transcripts
German or French language certificates (where needed)

CV, motivation letter and references
Visa application with embassies

fields.heading: Student Visa & Schengen Travel
items: Secure a university offer of admission

Apply for a national student visa at the embassy
Arrive and apply for a local residence permit
Travel freely across 27 Schengen countries during study

fields.title: NEB Class 12 Grade Increment Exam 2083: Best Official Guide
fields.excerpt: Everything you need to know about the Class 12 grade increment exam 2083 — dates, eligibility, steps, and how it impacts studying abroad.
fields.content:
The NEB Class 12 grade increment exam is your opportunity to improve your GPA by re-taking subjects you wish to upgrade. A stronger GPA directly improves your chances for competitive university admissions and scholarships abroad.

How to apply
You register through your college within the announced window. Keep your admit card, gradesheet and photocopies ready, and confirm the exact exam format with your institution coordinator.

Impact on study abroad applications
Australian, UK, EU and Canadian universities evaluate your overall academic record. Upgrading weak grades before you apply can move you from an average to a highly competitive profile — and our counsellors can advise exactly which subjects to re-take based on your target universities.

At Bristi, we help you plan around the increment exam timeline so your university applications are never delayed. Book a free counselling session to evaluate your GPA upgrade strategy.

fields.title: IELTS Test Preparation Guide for Nepali Students
fields.excerpt: A complete roadmap to scoring 7.0+ in IELTS — practice plans, common mistakes, and exam-day tips from our trainers.
fields.content:
Scoring well in IELTS requires more than practice — it requires a strategy. Here is our trusted roadmap for Nepali students targeting 6.5 to 7.5 band scores.

Listening
Listen to British, American and Australian accents daily. Practice note-taking under time pressure and always read the questions before the audio starts.

Reading
Learn skimming and scanning. Time is your biggest enemy, so build speed with daily timed passages instead of studying vocabulary lists alone.

Writing and Speaking
Memorise logical task structures (Task 1 data description and Task 2 essay frameworks). For speaking, record yourself, review fluency, and practise with a partner who corrects you.

Join our free IELTS mock test day to measure your current level and get a personalised band-score improvement plan.

fields.title: Student Visa Interview Tips for Nepal: What Visa Officers Check
fields.excerpt: Learn exactly what embassies evaluate in a student visa interview and how to answer like a prepared, genuine applicant.
fields.content:
A student visa interview is not about memory — it is about consistency. Visa officers evaluate whether your plan to study abroad is genuine.

What they check
1. Your reason for choosing the country, university and course.
2. Your financial capability and the source of funds.
3. Your realistic ties to Nepal and study-exit plans.

How to prepare
· Be honest about your academic profile and grades.
· Explain your career goal and how the course connects to it.
· Carry complete, organised financial documents.

Our visa counsellors conduct realistic mock interviews — book a free session and arrive at your interview genuinely confident.
fields.author: Bristi Team

fields.title: PTE Test in Nepal: Everything You Need to Know
fields.excerpt: Why more students are choosing PTE — faster results, AI scoring, and how to prepare effectively in Kathmandu.
fields.content:
The PTE Academic is becoming the test of choice for students targeting Australia, New Zealand, the UK and Canada — mainly because it delivers results within 48 hours.

How it differs from IELTS
PTE is fully computer-based and AI-scored, which removes human-subjectivity from speaking and writing sections. Many students find machine scoring more predictable once they understand the rubrics.

Preparation tips
· Master the integrated item types such as Read Aloud, Repeat Sentence and Summarise Spoken Text.
· Use the official scored mock test to pinpoint weak skills.
· Practise in real computer-lab conditions to build speed.

Our PTE class runs computer-based mocks every week — join us to start your journey with a free placement test.
fields.author: Bristi Team

fields.title: Study in Australia Guide: Intakes, Costs and Post-Study Work
fields.excerpt: Everything Nepali students must know before applying to Australia — intakes, tuition, scholarships and PR pathways.
fields.content:
Australia remains a top destination for Nepali students thanks to its high-quality universities, safe society and strong work rights.

Key facts
· Intakes are usually February and July.
· Post-study work rights range from two to four years depending on your qualification level.
· Tuition typically ranges from AUD 20,000 to 45,000 per year depending on the course.

Scholarship opportunities
Many universities award automatic scholarships of 10–25 percent for strong academic records. Our counsellors help you target institutions that maximise both scholarship and visa success.

Book your free counselling session to start planning the right intake and course for your profile.
fields.author: Bristi Team

fields.title: Study in Canada Guide: SDS, Co-ops and PR Pathways
fields.excerpt: A practical guide to studying in Canada — SDS visa stream, co-op programs, PGWP and the road to permanent residency.
fields.content:
Canada offers one of the clearest roads from student to permanent resident, which is why it remains one of Nepal's top destinations.

The SDS visa stream
The Student Direct Stream speeds up processing for applicants with IELTS and up-front tuition payment. Our counsellors verify your eligibility and help you assemble the complete dossier correctly.

Co-op and work opportunities
Many colleges integrate paid co-op terms into their programs, letting you graduate with Canadian work experience already on your CV.

After graduation, a Post-Graduation Work Permit of up to three years gives you time to qualify for permanent residency programs.

Speak with a Canadian specialist today to map your pathway.
